A Make.com workflow uses Google Docs, Gemini and Gmail to summarize documents, replacing manual copy-and-paste.
·

Done with
MK
Make
GE
Gemini
What they did
The poster built a simple Make.com workflow that connects Google Docs, Gemini, and Gmail. It pulls the content of a Google Doc, sends that text to Gemini to generate a summary, and then emails the summary through Gmail automatically; the human role described was setting up the flow as a replacement for manual copy-and-paste.
How it went
It worked as a first automation and helped the poster learn how the tools fit together for a repetitive task. The post gives no metrics, volume, or quality results, and it is presented as something still open to improvement.
Worth knowing
The main catch is that the source only describes the high-level flow, not trigger details, prompt design, error handling, cost, or timing.
Try it yourself
with
Make
Copy prompt
Build a Make scenario that watches [Google Drive folder] for new Google Docs, sends each document's text to Gemini to produce a [5-bullet] summary focused on [key decisions, action items, or risks], and emails the summary to [my address] through Gmail. Test it with one document and show me the email before you turn on scheduling. Done means a new doc in the folder automatically produces a correct summary email.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/AiAutomations/comments/1vkcum8/i_built_my_first_ai_automation_to_handle_a
